summary: Masahiro Shimoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Delhi, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023) and at Musashino University from 2023.
Masahiro Takano works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a librarian in 1995.

Masakatsu Fujita is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1968 to 1978 and later served there as head of the department of the History of Japanese Philosophy (circa 2001–2014).

Masakazu Tanaka is a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University and completed his Ph.D. at the University of London (LSE). He was an assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and became vice president and professor at the Professional Institute of International Fashion in 2019.

Masako Keta specializes in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi, later holding posts at Kanazawa University and serving as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University from 2000 to 2018.
Masamichi Asukai was a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1953 to 1957 and held a post there from circa 1970 to 1998.

Masamichi Ichigo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University, Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, and Michigan; he held posts at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Helmut Krasser in 2006.
Masanori Nakagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen University, where he is attested as a lecturer in 1991 and as an associate professor of literature in 2002.
Masanori Shono works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was attested as an assistant professor at Osaka University in 2012 and as a researcher at the University of Munich in 2015.

Masao Abe was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka City University, Kyoto University, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia University. He held professorships at Kyoto University, Nara University of Education, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Masao Shizutani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He served as an assistant professor at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, where he was attested in 1974.

Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held posts at Kyoto Women's University, including professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society, attested in 2002 and 2015.

Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He held academic posts there beginning in 1984, eventually serving as professor emeritus in 2017 and president in 2019.
Masataka Suzuki is a scholar of religious studies, history, and Japanology. He studied at Keio University from around 1968 to 1978 and served on its faculty from circa 1985 to 2015.

Masataro Sawayanagi studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1884–1888). He held posts at Tokyo University of Education (circa 1897–1898), Kyushu University (circa 1911–1912), Tohoku University (circa 1911–1913), and Taisho University (circa 1926–1927).

Masato Kobayashi specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, later serving as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (circa 2000–2004).

Masatoshi Konishi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at International Christian University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as an instructor of Sanskrit at Harvard University beginning in 1958.

Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (circa 1970–1979) and held academic posts at Kansai University (circa 1979–1988) and Osaka University (circa 1988–2017).
